data.topic: rust-anything (specs/z_external-repo-library/rust-anything-main, read-only) as a source for sk-code's Rust standards. Questions: (1) How is its own Rust written: Cargo.toml lints, edition and rust-version, module layout across src/, error handling, the clap CLI, serde settings, test layout and fixtures under tests/, and the cargo fmt, clippy and test finish gate in its CLAUDE.md? (2) What are its record, bridge, diff, bench, shadow and gate method (docs/how-it-works.md), docs/pitfalls.md and DECISIONS.md, and which of them apply to any Rust port checked against an original? (3) How does docs/types.md map values across napi-rs, PyO3, the C ABI and the other bridges? (4) How do skills/rust-anything/SKILL.md and whole-app.md steer a coding agent through a port? (5) For each finding, does the existing sk-code Rust set under .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-skilled/references/rust/ and assets/checklists/rust-checklist/ cover it, contradict it or lack it, by file and section, and what does an app-style Rust project such as a CLI or a ratatui terminal screen need that the set lacks? Cite file:line for every claim. End with a ranked edit list, each naming the target sk-code Rust part, the change and the rust-anything source line.
